finding.evidence: ReleaseButton is rendered for locked decisions in admin/applications/[id]/page.tsx:552 and Hash (source references inspected). It calls useAction/runAction, which awaits authorizedFetch and response.json without a deadline, accepts every successful HTTP response including a null/malformed body, and maps transport loss to 'Could not release'. Only result.ok or released:true triggers refresh. The batch release tests in release-reliability.spec.ts exercise ReleaseAllButton, so their lost/stalled coverage does not cover this live alternative.
finding.userImpact: A stalled single release can remain at Releasing indefinitely. A committed release followed by response loss leaves a stale locked row and generic failure with retry available; a malformed successful response can announce release without a verified receipt. Operators receive different certainty for the same irreversible outcome depending on entry point.
finding.suggestedFix: Give single release the same bounded full-body wait, validated action-specific receipt, explicit unknown-outcome feedback and authoritative readback as batch release. Add focused single-release stalled-body, malformed-success and commit-then-lost-response checks.

finding.evidence: save() awaits authorizedFetch through retryOnNetworkError at lines 157–162 without a deadline, including response.json(). The helper in src/lib/client-fetch.ts retries rejected requests but does not bound unresolved requests. Every later save for that applicant waits on inflight.current at line 149; its resolver runs only in finally. Consequently, stalled headers or body consumption can keep the row at Saving indefinitely and prevent newer changes from reaching the server. The retry/copy guidance at roster lines 419–424 is rendered only for error/hint states. group-case-evidence.spec.ts covers rejected saves and a delayed receipt that eventually resolves, rather than a never-settling response. This is a source-derived path, not a hosted reproduction.
finding.userImpact: A reviewer can continue entering observations while the save queue remains blocked, with no bounded route to recover or explicit copy-before-leaving guidance during the stalled saving state. Reloading can discard those in-memory changes.
finding.suggestedFix: Bound the complete acknowledgement lifecycle, expose an unknown-save state with private copy/export recovery, and reconcile safely before permitting replacement writes so delayed commits cannot overwrite newer evidence. Add stalled-header/body cases that verify queued edits remain recoverable and no false saved receipt appears.
